title: Authorization bypass via the filer `?proxyChunkId=` branch dispatching ahead of the JWT gate, enabling unauthenticated chunk read and deletion
summary:
## Summary

An **Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key (CWE-639) / Missing Authentication for a Critical Function (CWE-306)** in the SeaweedFS filer: the `?proxyChunkId=` chunk-proxy branch in `filerHandler` is dispatched and returned before `maybeCheckJwtAuthorization` runs, so `GET`, `PUT`, `POST` and `DELETE` against any needle in the cluster are reachable on the filer's HTTP port with no filer credential of any kind - on a filer where `jwt.filer_signing.key` and `jwt.filer_signing.read.key` are both configured and every other request answers `401 wrong jwt`. An unauthenticated caller reads the bytes of a stored object, replaces them, or deletes the needle; the deletion becomes unrecoverable at the master's next routine garbage vacuum. A second, independent exemption in the same function serves `GET /` - the filer root listing, including `chunks[].file_id` for every file at the root - to the same unauthenticated caller, which supplies the fid the proxy branch needs.

This is an incomplete fix of the hardening in #10434 (`91979ec51`), whose own commit message names the attack: *"The `?proxyChunkId=` branch dispatches and returns before the JWT gate, so whatever credential the proxy attaches is reachable without authentication. … An anonymous `DELETE /?proxyChunkId=<fid>` therefore arrived at the volume server holding a write-key token scoped to that fid, and the volume server honored it."* That change stopped the filer from minting a write-key token for an anonymous caller. It did not stop the anonymous caller from reaching the volume server, and where the volume server has no `jwt.signing.key` of its own - the shipped default, and the configuration `weed/command/scaffold/security.toml` describes for a filer deployment - the anonymous DELETE still lands.

## Affected component

`weed/server/filer_server_handlers.go`, `filerHandler` lines 58-79 and `maybeCheckJwtAuthorization` lines 213-219; `weed/server/filer_server_handlers_proxy.go`, `proxyToVolumeServerURL`. Confirmed at release `4.45` (`79b87202136cebdaaa7db4d94eaa5915ad381276`) and at `master` `9fef11526e6a3b59ebffa42a1a31f2f7d425b595`; the two files are byte-identical between them. The proxy branch has existed since the endpoint was added; the `GET /` exemption was added by `6940b7d06` (2026-01-29) for health checks, before the filer had `/healthz` and `/readyz`.

## Deployment and attacker position

The deployment is the one GHSA-gv5w-hfx8-8cwq (CVE-2026-72921) and GHSA-99q7-x53r-6j4g (CVE-2026-77368) were both filed against: master, volume server and filer running, only the filer's HTTP port reachable by the attacker, internal master and volume ports private, and `jwt.filer_signing` / `jwt.filer_signing.read` configured so the filer accepts no unsigned request. The attacker holds no credential at all. The volume server's own `jwt.signing.key` is unset, which is the shipped default and what the scaffold recommends for a filer - its comment on `jwt.signing.read` reads *"jwt for read is only supported with master+volume setup. Filer does not support this mode."*

## Details

`filerHandler` reads `proxyChunkId` off `/` and dispatches on it before it reaches the authorization gate:

```go
	// proxy to volume servers
	var fileId string
	if r.URL.Path == "/" {
		fileId = r.URL.Query().Get("proxyChunkId")
	}
	if fileId != "" {
		fs.proxyToVolumeServer(w, r, fileId)
		...
		return                                   // returns before the gate below
	}
	...
	isReadHttpCall := r.Method == http.MethodGet || r.Method == http.MethodHead
	if !fs.maybeCheckJwtAuthorization(r, !isReadHttpCall) {
		writeJsonError(w, r, http.StatusUnauthorized, errors.New("wrong jwt"))
		return
	}
```

There is no method restriction on the branch, so a `PUT`, `POST` or `DELETE` is proxied to the volume server exactly as a `GET` is, with the caller's body and query forwarded. On a read the filer additionally mints a fid-scoped volume read token on the caller's behalf (`maybeGetVolumeReadJwtA...
